questions.solution: The correct answer is option 3) i.e., **'****With a magnifying glass'. ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The underlined part is grammatically incorrect as **it is missing an article.** • In the given sentence, we need to use an **indefinite **article in the underlined part before the **gerund 'magnifying' **as the specific identity of the 'magnifying glass' is not established. • We need to use the **indefinite article 'a' **before the word **magnifying **since the word **magnifying **starts with a **consonant. ** • Hence, option 3 is the correct answer. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** • रेखांकित भाग व्याकरणिक रूप से गलत है क्योंकि इसमें article नहीं है। • दिए गए वाक्य में, हमें gerund 'magnifying' से पहले रेखांकित भाग में एक indefinite article का उपयोग करने की आवश्यकता है क्योंकि **'magnifying glass'**** **की विशिष्ट पहचान स्थापित नहीं की गई है। • Magnifying शब्द से पहले हमें indefinite article 'a' का उपयोग करने की आवश्यकता है क्योंकि magnifying शब्द एक व्यंजन के साथ शुरू होता है। • अतः **विकल्प 3** सही उत्तर है। 2f:Tbdc, The correct answer is **option 2)i.e., 'The policeman said that it was clear that this was the work of a professional robber.'**

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.**

The policeman said, “It is clear that this is the work of a professional robber”

options.text: The policeman said that it had been clearly the work of a professional robber.
The policeman said that it was clear that this was the work of a professional robber.
The policeman said it was clear that is the work of a professional robber.
The policeman said that it must be clear that this was the work of a professional robber.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2)i.e., 'The policeman said that it was clear that this was the work of a professional robber.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech.**
 
• While changing the narration of **an assertive sentence**, we need to follow steps.
 
 
• The** reporting verb 'said' remains unchanged.**
 
• The **conjunction 'that'** is used in place of commas and inverted commas. 
 
• The **verb (is)** is in the **simple present tense form** in the given sentence. In the indirect speech, **‘is’ changes into ‘was’. ** 

 ​
 
 

Eventually, we will get the final sentence- " The policeman said that it was clear that this was the work of a professional robber."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• 
 
In direct speeches, the words that express nearness in time or place are changed to words that express distance in indirect speech. Such as :

 
 
• 
 
Now becomes then, Here becomes there, Ago becomes before, Thus becomes so, Today becomes that day, Tomorrow becomes the next day, This becomes that, Yesterday becomes the day before, These become those, Hither becomes thither, Come becomes go, Hence becomes thence, Next week or month becomes the following week/month.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Hence, in the given sentence, 'this' is a pronoun that is not referring to time or place hence, 'this' will not be changed.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.**

Suresh has only been working __here since one month__ and he has already learnt the job.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e., 'here for one month'. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The underlined part is grammatically incorrect as it uses the incorrect preposition 'since'. 
 
• We use **since **with a point in time in the past. E.g. - It was the band's first live performance **since May 1990.**
 
• The correct **preposition, in this case,** is **for. **
 
• We use **for** with a period of time in the past, present or future. E.g. - She's been on the phone **for hours.**

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Shopkeeper: “Here, I have packed them all.”

B. Mala: “Please give me a packet of balloons, two packets of streamers, and some candles.”

C. Shopkeeper: “Since we are offering some discount on the balloons, you need to pay only thirty rupees.”

D. Mala: “How much do I need to pay?”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The conversation starts with Mala’s request for the items she wants to purchase, which is initiated in **Sentence B**.
 
• The **Sentence A** follows as it shows the shopkeeper confirming that the items have been packed.
 
• The **Sentence D** is next because Mala asks how much she needs to pay after the items are packed.
 
• Finally, **Sentence C** provides the cost of the balloons, adding further details about the payment.
 
• The correct order is **BADC**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:**

Mala: "Please give me a packet of balloons, two packets of streamers, and some candles." Shopkeeper: "Here, I have packed them all." Mala: "How much do I need to pay?" Shopkeeper: "Since we are offering some discount on the balloons, you need to pay only thirty rupees."

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. They stopped at a village on the way to rest and drink water and found the entire village had gathered to watch a weightlifter who was putting on a performance.

B. Tenali was very impressed and exclaimed, “You are very strong!”

C. With his big arms and bulging muscles, he picked up a 200-kg bag of rice with ease.

D. One day Tenali Raman and his wife were on their way to Hampi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e., ‘DACB’.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly.
 
• The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 
 
• Here, only D is independent and introduce a topic of how the subjects Tenali Raman and his wife were going to Hampi. 
 
• It should be followed by **A ** which talks about what they did on their journey towards Hampi. 
 
• So, A must come after D. Then DA is the correct order.
 
• This order is shown in option 4, which shows the full sequence as: DACB.

Thus, the correct sequence is: DACB

**D.** One day Tenali Raman and his wife were on their way to Hampi.

**A. **They stopped at a village on the way to rest and drink water and found the entire village had gathered to watch a weightlifter who was putting on a performance.

**C.** With his big arms and bulging muscles, he picked up a 200-kg bag of rice with ease.

**B.** Tenali was very impressed and exclaimed, “You are very strong!”

options.text: on the banks of or near large rivers

Correct sentence - *Four of **the **earliest civilisations of the world were located on the banks of or near large rivers.*

• We use **a superlative** to say that a thing or person is the most of a group.
 
• When we use a **superlative adjective ('the tallest student') **before the noun, we generally **use it with 'the'.**
 
• This is because there's only one (or one group) of the thing we are talking about.
 
• There is one student who is the tallest in the class, and because it's clear to the listener which one we mean, we usually use '**the**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Following these steps, we finally get - " The neighbour's window was broken by the boy's cricket ball."

__
 
• The given blank needs the **preposition of. **

• Thus, 'emissions' is the best-fit word for the given blank.
 
• This makes option 3 the correct answer.
